# Summarise gene expression at the gene level by summing up expression of each transcript

```{r, summarise-exp}

if(subs=="all"){
#tx_to_gene <- annot_host_final |> dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id)
tx_to_gene <- annot_combined |> 
  dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id)
#optional: could try to use the "final" annot_combined object produced above.
#tx_to_gene <- annot_combined_final |> dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id)

salmon_gene_quants <-
  salmon_df |>
  dplyr::select(sample_name, transcript_id = Name, n_reads = NumReads, tpm = TPM) |>
  left_join(tx_to_gene, join_by(transcript_id)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample_name, gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(across(c(n_reads, tpm), sum), .groups = "drop")  #new
  }else if(subs=="host"){
tx_to_gene <- annot_host |> dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id)
salmon_gene_quants <-
  salmon_df |>
  dplyr::filter(Name %in% c(c_dna_h, nc_rna_h)) |>
  dplyr::select(sample_name, transcript_id = Name, n_reads = NumReads, tpm = TPM) |>
  left_join(tx_to_gene, join_by(transcript_id)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample_name, gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(across(c(n_reads, tpm), sum), .groups = "drop")  #new
  }else if(subs=="host_cdna"){
tx_to_gene <- annot_host |> dplyr::filter(transcript_id %in% c_dna_h) |> dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id)  
salmon_gene_quants <-
  salmon_df |>
  dplyr::filter(Name %in% c_dna_h) |>
  dplyr::select(sample_name, transcript_id = Name, n_reads = NumReads, tpm = TPM) |>
  left_join(tx_to_gene, join_by(transcript_id)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample_name, gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(across(c(n_reads, tpm), sum), .groups = "drop")  #new  
  }else if(subs=="virus"){
tx_to_gene <- annot_virus |> dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id)  
salmon_gene_quants <-
  salmon_df |>
  dplyr::filter(Name %in% c_dna_v) |>
  dplyr::select(sample_name, transcript_id = Name, n_reads = NumReads, tpm = TPM) |>
  left_join(tx_to_gene, join_by(transcript_id)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample_name, gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(across(c(n_reads, tpm), sum), .groups = "drop")
}
```

# Run DESeq
```{r, deseq}

ddsTxi <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromTximport(
  txi = txi, colData = coldata, design= ~ condition + batch)

#similar but stated differently
#ddsTxi2 <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromTximport(
#     txi = txi, colData = coldata, 
#     design= ~ virus + timePt + treatment + treatment:virus + virus:timePt + treatment:virus:timePt + batch)
#Question 3: why is rowData names(0). is this ok or does it indicate something went wrong? What is the differences between rownames and rowData names?
#Vitor's answer: it seems normal, rowData seems to apply to other tyeps of objects from bioconductor. 
####################
##optional filtering
####################
#filter <- which(rowSums(counts(ddsTxi))>=10) # 31652
#smallestGroupSize <- 5
#keep <- which(rowSums(counts(ddsTxi) >= 10)>= smallestGroupSize) #28423 rows
#Question 4: where do I filter these out suing the current code? DESeq(counts(ddsTxi)[filter,])? Note: Before I was using a different approach (see Upenn code at the bottom of this report).
#Vitor's answer: i don't normally do this filtering and instead let DESEQ do the independent filtering, which is an algorithm to remove genes based on expression level with the aim of maximizing power. But if wanted use: 
#keep<-rowSums(counts(dds)>=count_thresh) >=n_samples; dds<-dds[keep,]


dds_combined <- DESeq2::DESeq(object = ddsTxi, parallel = T)
#9 rows did not converge in beta, labelled in mcols(object)$betaConv. Use larger maxit argument with nbinomWaldTest

#dds_combined2 <- DESeq2::DESeq(object = ddsTxi2, parallel = T)
#221 rows did not converge in beta, labelled in mcols(object)$betaConv. Use larger maxit argument with nbinomWaldTest

#-------Results

#contrasts available by default

DESeq2::resultsNames(dds_combined) 
#Question 5: 15 contrasts here? Why?
#dds_combined_res <- DESeq2::results(dds_combined)
#Question 6: if I don't specific any contrasts here, why is the one returned an arbitrary conteast based on the design I provided? I.e., in this case here the object is:

#dds_combined_res # batch b5 vs b1 

#vitor's answers to 5 and 6: you can find this in the ?DESeq2::results page:
#"If results is run without specifying contrast or name, it will return the comparison of the last level of the last variable in the design formula over the first level of this variable."
#DESeq2::resultsNames(dds_combined2) 

#what rows are they?
#Identify problematic genes


failed_conv<-as.data.frame(mcols(dds_combined)) |>
  dplyr::filter(betaConv==F) %>% rownames() #7

#inspect them
failed_conv
#inspect them
annot_combined |> 
  dplyr::filter(gene_id %in% failed_conv) #all are host genes

#inspecting their counts
head(counts(dds_combined)[failed_conv,]) 
#total nr reads mapped across samples for these failed genes

#BDB: Vitor doesn't think we need to filter out these genes. 
```

```{r, plots, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 12}
#colors

DESeq2::plotDispEsts(dds_combined)
dev.off()
#plotDispEsts(dds_combined) #for report
#Question 7: not sure what I should be looking for here. I saw this in the tutorials and Upenn code.
#Vitor's answer: I never really look at these plots except when I was first studying deseq. I trust DESeq to deal with this relationship between expression elvel and variance and to correct that properly in normalizations such as vst(). 

#######################################################################################
# Plot PCA with PCAtools
#######################################################################################

# calculate principle components and annotate samples

#Question 8: is this the right way to do this? I am using vst because Upenn did that but I think you had suggested something different?
#Vitor's answer: it looks right. I don't remember what assay(vst(dds)) does. If compatible with the function you're using, perfect. I use DESeq2::plotPCA(vst(dds), ntop = 2000, returnData = TRUE)
mat<-assay(vst(dds_combined))
metadata <- colData(dds_combined)
identical(rownames(metadata),colnames(mat))
p <- PCAtools::pca(
            mat = mat,
           # metadata = colData(dds_host_res),
            metadata = metadata,
           removeVar = 0.5) #  fraction of low variance data to exclude

# Question 9: what value to use for removeVar?ccc
# Vitor's answer: there is no value; it's arbitrary.You can plot expression levels vs variance to try to find an appropriate value for your date. Single-cell RNA-seq folks usually do that. E.g.:https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/pbmc3k_tutorial.html#identification-of-highly-variable-features-feature-selection
# write table of PC coordinates for each sample for use in external graphing tools
#system("mkdir PC_rnk_files")


ld <- as_tibble(getLoadings(p), rownames = "#geneID")

for (i in 1:4) {
  write_tsv(file = paste0("new_results/new_PC_rnk_files/PC",i,"_loadings",ext, ".rnk"), dplyr::select(ld, c(1,i+1)))
  head(dplyr::select(ld, c(1,i+1)))
}



# integrate symbols where possible for gene labels

rownames(p$loadings) <- as_tibble(rownames(p$loadings)) |>
  setNames("gene_id") |>
  #left_join(annot_dds_host) |>
  left_join(annot_combined) |>
  
  dplyr::select(c("gene_id")) |>
  unique() |>
  deframe() 

##########################
# SCREE plot (variation per component)

pdf(file = paste0("new_results/new_plots/PCAscreeplot_",ext,".pdf"),
    width = 12,
    height = 12)

PCAtools::screeplot(p, axisLabSize = 15, titleLabSize = 20)
dev.off()
PCAtools::screeplot(p, axisLabSize = 12, titleLabSize = 15) #for report

    width = 12,
    height = 12)

          colby = "condition")

dev.off()

PCAtools::pairsplot(p,
          colby = "condition") # for report
```

```{r, upenn1, eval = F, echo = F}
# Upenn code - here for reference and because I used it for PCAs earlier this week but not being run in this doc.

#Question 10: any advantage in using parts of their code?

################################
# If using non-gencode data, then need this (first time) for tximeta
################################

indexDir="~/Documents/rosalind-rna-seq-mirror/salmonq_all/j_decoy7/decoyIndex"

fastaFTP<-"~/Documents/rosalind-rna-seq-mirror/salmonq_all/j_decoy7/gentrome.fa.gz"

gtfPath_h <- c(
  "https://ftp.ensemblgenomes.ebi.ac.uk/pub/protists/release-60/gff3/emiliania_huxleyi/Emiliania_huxleyi.Emiliana_huxleyi_CCMP1516_main_genome_assembly_v1.0.60.gff3.gz")
tximeta::makeLinkedTxome(
  indexDir = indexDir,
  source = "LocalEnsembl",
  organism = "Emiliania huxleyi",
  release = "113",
  genome = "EhCCMP1516",
  fasta = fastaFTP,
  gtf = gtfPath_h,
  write = TRUE,
  jsonFile = "EhCCMP1516_113.tximeta.json"
)


# Then for future runs just load tx database with json file

# get correct metadata automatically

se_host <- tximeta::tximeta(coldata,
                            type = "salmon",
                            skipMeta = F,
                            useHub = TRUE)
```
